The [[Cipango (system)|Cipango system]] is a [[System|star system]].
* It consists of a central [[star]], its family of [[world]]s, and their [[Natural Satellite|various moons]].
* The [[system]]'s [[mainworld]] is [[Cipango (world)|Cipango]].

== Description ([[Astrography]] & [[Planetology]]) == 
=== Stellar Data ===
They '''Cipango system''' has a solitary primary star.
* It is a yellow main sequence named ''Cipango-Taiyoo''.

{{MonostellarSystem
|name           = Cipango
|primary        = G2 V
|PrimaryName    = Cipango-Taiyoo
|PrimaryNotes   = 
}}

=== System Data ===
The worlds of the [[system]] have been surveyed. They consist of:
* The [[mainworld]].
* x6 secondary [[world|rocky worlds]]. The inner three are a large [[Inner World|inner system]] [[planetoid]] named ''Himawari'', tropical ''Kusai'', and tiny ''Doitsu'', lying beyond Cipango's orbit. Three additional unnamed frozen worlds orbit in the [[Outer World|far outer system]].
* x2 [[planetoid belt]]s, named the ''Zero-Belt'', orbiting close to the star, and the ''Yon-Belt'', lying between Cipango and Doitsu.
* x1 [[gas giant]], named ''Fukuzawa''. It orbits beyond Doitsu, in the [[Outer World|outer system]].
** It retains a family of [[Natural Satellite|three moons]].

The Cipango system is not very impressive, but it still has three garden worlds: Kusai, Cipango itself, and Tsuki-Shivva, Cipango's moon.

Kusai orbits within the inner part of the [[habitable zone]]. Its climate is [[Celsius|a little too hot]] for human comfort, the atmosphere has a foul smell, and there is dangerous [[Lifeform|local wildlife]], so it has not attracted a large population. It orbits within the star's [[Jump Shadow]], so it is rarely visited by interstellar traders.

Cipango itself has a large moon, Tsuki-Shivva, which has been colonized. It is considered a fairly nice place that has a cooler climate than Cipango itself. Most of the new colonists from the Consulate have settled here.

== History & Background (Dossier) ==
Fukuzawa, the system's solitary [[gas giant]], has [[Natural Satellite|three moons]]. These are F-8 (the innermost, orbiting at 8 radii,) and the twin moons of ''F-11 prim'' and ''F-11 bis'' (both orbiting at 11 radii, but with 60 degrees separation between them). All three are cold, airless chunks of rock.
